title: BetFirm Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: BetFirm review, checked 17 Nov 2026: Jack Jones's pick storefront, prices from $19.99 picks to $1,999.95 a year, how the guarantee works and what buyers say.
dek: A picks and betting articles site that says Jack Jones founded it in 2003. It lists about 27 handicappers, led by Jones, and every Buy Now button sends you to the SportsCapping.com cart. Prices run from $19.99 for one pick to $1,999.95 for a year, guarantees pay in free picks, not cash, and the records come from the same network that sells the picks.

short_answer: BetFirm is a working storefront. It posts prices, shows the picks each handicapper released yesterday with the result, and hands buyers to the SportsCapping.com checkout, a marketplace that names Boyd Information Group as its billing company. BetFirm itself names no company, address or phone number, and we found no terms or refund page on the site.

Its sales copy is built on long runs and rankings, such as Jack Jones's "No. 2 Ranked Overall Capper All-Time!" Those rankings come from the same network that sells the picks. On BetFirm's own current year leaderboard, Jones was up $821 on $100 bets, a 0.4% return, which is close to break even before the cost of the picks.
We found no independent buyer reviews of BetFirm at all. Treat it as a store with marketing records, not a source of proven winners.

guarantee: BetFirm's guarantee wording is sales copy on each package. The 7 day pass says: "You are GUARANTEED PROFITS or the next 7 days of premium picks in all sports is ON JACK!" In plain words, if the pass loses you get another 7 days of picks. You do not get your money back, and it never covers what you lost on the bets.

Because checkout happens on SportsCapping.com, the SportsCapping rules apply. Its FAQ says "refunds are reviewed individually", that losing guaranteed packages earn a free replacement on their own, and that credits "can't be withdrawn or exchanged for cash." Its Terms of Use provide the service "as is", send disputes to courts in Iowa and limit claims to one year.

claims_note: The headline runs and the leaderboard tell different stories. The sales copy for Jack Jones cites a run of 7,334 wins and 6,415 losses with $311,670 won by $1,000 bettors. BetFirm's own current year leaderboard shows Jones at 904 and 811, up $821 on $100 bets, a 0.4% return. Both may be accurate; one is a long chosen window and the other is this year.

The Best Handicappers page says it shows "the documented records for all of our handicappers for the current year." All 27 rows in the table we read showed a profit. We could not tell whether losing handicappers are left out or whether every handicapper happened to be ahead.
Profit is shown in dollars on $100 or $1,000 bets. It does not subtract the price of the picks, which at $34.95 a play or $1,999.95 a year can be larger than the betting profit shown.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing we could find. We found no full, time stamped log kept by an outside monitor and no contest result we could open.

What BetFirm publishes: a current year leaderboard and a long term "Top Trends" table for about 27 handicappers, plus a yesterday's plays table on each handicapper page. On 17 Nov 2026 Jones's table showed his 20 star Ravens play from the night before as a loss. The leaderboard uses the SportsCapping "Sc Score" column, so these numbers come from the selling network, not a separate grader.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no BetFirm handicapper is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these handicappers perform.
our_data.context: For scale: BetFirm's own current year leaderboard tops out near 57% for handicappers with a few hundred picks. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: We found no independent buyer review of BetFirm. CapperTek lists both BetFirm.com and BetFirms.com with no reviews. The Reddit search for this page was partial: the Arctic Shift archive's full text search timed out for most queries on 17 Nov 2026, so we used a local copy of earlier Reddit downloads and the few queries that returned. The entries below are what exists.

customers.text: There is almost no buyer talk about BetFirm as a business. Review sites list it with zero reviews, the Reddit archive queries that returned found no post about it, and web searches found no forum thread reviewing it. The only outside mention we found was a TheRX member reposting Jack Jones plays in April 2026, without comment on results. With no positive or negative buyer reports, the record question rests on the network's own numbers.
A member of a TheRX daily plays thread posted seven Jack Jones plays for the day with their star ratings. The post gives no view on his results or on buying from BetFirm.

CapperTek lists BetFirm.com and BetFirms.com, both with no reviews or complaints. The Arctic Shift queries that returned found no Reddit discussion of BetFirm. We found no Sportsbook Review, Covers or TheRX thread reviewing the site, no BBB profile under the BetFirm name, and we did not read Trustpilot.

conflicts: BetFirm's founder is also its top selling handicapper and its editor in chief, and its rankings come from the SportsCapping network that processes the sales. Every link in the chain earns from the sale.
Buy Now links carry an affiliate code into the SportsCapping cart, so BetFirm is paid as a referral storefront for the network.
BetFirm names no company of its own. A buyer with a problem has to deal with SportsCapping and Boyd Information Group, which the BetFirm pages do not explain.
strengths: Prices are posted for every package.
Each handicapper page shows yesterday's plays with the result, losses included.
Lots of free material: a daily free pick, betting guides and odds pages.
The checkout company has a BBB profile showing one complaint in the last three years.
concerns: No company name, address, phone, terms or refund page on BetFirm itself.
Records and rankings come from the network that sells the picks. No outside monitor found.
Sales copy leans on long chosen runs, while the current year leaderboard shows Jones near break even.
Guarantees pay in more picks, not cash.
No independent buyer reviews at all, positive or negative.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, odds and send time. A long run with a chosen start date is not a record.
Subtract the price of the picks from any profit figure before you compare.
Read each package's guarantee line. Not every pass has one, and none pays cash.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner.
faq: It is a working storefront that delivers picks through the SportsCapping.com checkout, and it says Jack Jones founded it in 2003. It names no company of its own, and we could not verify that its handicappers win over time, because the records come from the network that sells the picks.
On 17 Nov 2026 Jack Jones single picks cost $34.95 to $39.95, a 1 day pass $59.95 and a 365 day pass $1,999.95. Bobby Conn picks started at $19.99.

The About page says Jack Jones established it in 2003 and lists him as editor in chief. Payments go through SportsCapping.com, whose FAQ says purchases show on card statements as Boyd Information Group.

Only if a handicapper shows a profit over hundreds of picks after the price of the picks. Jones's own current year line on the site was up $821 on $100 bets, about a 0.4% return, before paying for the picks.
